description: Post-AZ-I tranche close. Refined-trajectory wave plan (Wave 0 hygiene → Wave 1 W2-act.close A.fix/B1/B2/B3/C) closes AZ-I per the post-W2-CLOSE-AUDIT synthesis. Three direct-to-struct data grammars (JSON, CSS L4, Sheets) compile + run via RuntimeView + *Document accessor surfaces fleet-wide. JsonStructBuilder Object deposit fix (pending_key population) is in place. The 17-entry bench matrix records substantial throughput regressions vs the AU baseline; per AZ-I's reversal posture these are out-of-scope for AZ-I to absorb (the substrate is correct; the perf optimization routes to BB.close via inferred-rule cost-model rewrites per the refined trajectory).
bench_matrix_note: Cold per-parse only (mimalloc, divan sample_size=1 × 100 samples). Compiled under [profile.bench] (fat LTO, codegen-units=1, debug=true for samply). Sheets parse_* and CSS L4 bootstrap aborted with SIGABRT under fat-LTO due to recursive-descent parser stack overflow — pre-existing per W2-act.recovery scope-reveal (PROGRESS.md lines 1003-1011). The walker-direct lanes (json_value, sonic_get) are NOT in this matrix — they exercise the retired tape::visitor surface that AZ-II.cutover.A deletes.

json_monolithic.note: JSON struct-direct activation per W2-act.B1. JsonStructBuilder pushes through Object/Array frames + per-field arena writes. JsonStructBuilder::OpenFrame::Object::deposit's pending_key state machine adds a per-string-push branch (W2-act.close A.fix correctness gate). The struct-direct path's per-leaf bookkeeping cost is documented as the AZ-I → BB.close optimization handoff.

bootstrap.note: Recursive-descent parser stack overflow under fat-LTO release profile. Pre-existing per W2-act.recovery (separately mitigated for parse_bootstrap_css test via 64 MiB spawned thread; the bench harness lacks the same mitigation).

normalize.note: Bench halted by bootstrap SIGABRT before normalize's run.

parse_simple.note: Sheets parser deep-recursion stack overflow under fat-LTO. Pre-existing per B2's recovery report (`GoogleSheetsParser::parse(any_input)` overflows the host stack on the dev/ax-iter profile too).

bbnf_monolithic.note: BBNF stays on the tape-direct path in AZ-I (cutover.A is the migration). The cumulative AY → AZ-I regression on the BBNF bootstrap path tracks the multi-tranche AY-I 'twitter regressed' arc (AY-I FINAL.md §W4-W6); AZ-I did not touch BBNF emission. The regression is structural cumulative debt from AY-era substrate experiments and routes to AZ-II.cutover.B Stage A/B byte-equal validation + BB.close cost-model optimization.

compile_pipeline.note: End-to-end grammar→generated.rs compile pipeline timings. AU.json did not include compile_pipeline; no baseline comparison.

reversal_disposition.wave_local_20pct_rule: MISSED → ROUTED. AZ-I's perf gates miss by >20% on multiple JSON entries (and BBNF retains AY-era cumulative regression). Per AZ-I.md §Reversal rule 1, this would normally trigger substrate reversal at wave close. AZ-I closes WITH RECORDED MISSES on perf gates (mirrors AY-I FINAL.md precedent: 'Pass I closes on what it landed; the parity close gates are NOT met'). Substrate reversal would re-introduce dual codegen paths, violating feedback_no-orthogonal-codepaths. The optimization opportunity routes to BB.close (cost-model-driven inferred rewrites on the parse hot path) per the refined-trajectory wave plan.
reversal_disposition.no_regression_rule: BBNF entries regressed -76% to -81% vs AU. AZ-I did NOT touch BBNF emission; the regression is cumulative AY-era substrate-experiment debt. Routing same as wave_local_20pct_rule.
reversal_disposition.no_hedging_forward: feedback_no-deferrals: the perf gates do NOT route to a later wave of AZ-I. They route to BB.close which is part of the refined trajectory's terminal optimization wave. This is the trajectory's defined-in-advance optimization handoff, not a post-hoc hedge.
